identity.title: An extraction-free one-pot immunomagnetic-RPA-CRISPR/Cas13a platform for ultrasensitive detection of exosomal PD-L1.

content.abstract: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expressed on the surface of exosomes (exo) is a promising liquid biopsy biomarker for monitoring response to immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, existing detection methods are limited by insufficient sensitivity and complicated operation. To address this, we developed an extraction-free immunomagnetic recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA)-based one-pot high-sensitivity CRISPR/Cas13a platform (iMRO-HCRISPR) employing DNA-conjugated antibodies. Exosomes in blood were enriched with anti-CD63/CD81/CD9 antibody-conjugated magnetic beads and recognized by PD-L1-specific DNA-antibody probes; the probe DNA then underwent RPA amplification, in vitro transcription (IVT), and Cas13a trans-cleavage, achieving multi-level signal amplification with fluorescent readout. Toehold-mediated DNA affinity pull-down effectively reduced the detection background. The platform achieved a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 10(1) particles/mL (positive detection at the single-particle level), a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 10(3) particles/mL, and a quantitative range of 10(3)-10(11) particles/mL, with the entire process completed in a single closed tube without exosome isolation. Clinical validation demonstrated that the platform effectively distinguished HCC patients from healthy controls (P < 0.0001), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.964. This study provides robust technical support for the ultrasensitive detection of exosomal PD-L1 in HCC and for dynamic monitoring of immunotherapy response.
